Rising Star Dancer Andile

By: Diana Lucas | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
He's dancing as fast as he can meet Andile Ndlovu...a fast rising star with the Washington Ballet

Summary:
Meet Andile Ndlovu, a fast-rising star with the Washington Ballet. His dancing teachers say his culture inspires his art - and his roots lie deep in the dust of a South African township. Carte Blanche takes to the dance floor in the arms of a young man with magic in the tips of his toes. We met him in 2008...now Andile has danced his way to further success. We travel to New York and spend time with one of SA's great dancers .

Press Release:


Andile Ndlovu
From the dance halls of Soweto, to centre stage at the Washington Ballet, Andile Ndlovu’s got magic in the tips of
his toes and he’s dancing his way into the hearts of ballet aficionados. Now, almost a decade since we first met
Ndlovu, who left South Africa in 2008 to pursue a career as an international ballet dancer, Carte Blanche catches up
with him in New York City.

Script:


Andile: The dream was still there to go overseas so I had to jump for it I had to take the chance and started from the beginning re building myself and moulding myself into a new dancer.

V/O
Young and passionate, 29 year old Andile Ndlovu is a dancer at the Washington Ballet. Andile arrived in America nine years ago on a ballet scholarship and walking around the Lincoln Centre in New York, with him it’s clear he’ feels part of this extraordinary city

LINK
We first met AD in 2008 he was already a rising star he was on his way to America to take up a prestigious spot at the Washington Ballet School

Andile Ndlovu

Andile : When we met you it was 5 days before you left South Africa for Washington?
Yes there was young Andile very bright and looking forward to tackling the challenges that the world has has for him.

V/O
Andile was 10 years old when he started training in Latin American and Ballroom Dance. The reason, really because there was no soccer club near where they lived in Ennerdale. His mother Thembi enrolled him at the Ennerdale Dance Academy.

Thembi Ndlovu
Andile’s Mother
Thembi: One day my daughter told me you know what Mummy there is nothing else we can do but there is Ballroom Dance at the Community Hall and we are busy trying to get Andile doing that but Andile had no interest at all.

Nqobile Ndlovu
Andile’s sister
I had to pay him to go and dance then I had to beg him I will wash the dishes for you, and I will give you R2 or R4 of my spending just to go and he just walked in an knocked it off like that.

Andile: As I started dancing I don’t know a bug hit me, it started from then.

V/O
When he was 15, Andile was discovered by the Ballet Theatre Afrikan and given a bursary.

LINK
Studying ballet in a city like NY or Washington sounds perfectly normal but when you are growing up in a township it’s a tough choice

V/O
…and despite his growing success in the world of ballet, Andile found the perception of male ballet dancers hard to live with.

Andile: I had 2 faces so when I went to Highland North Boys I lived a whole year in that’s school and they didn’t even know I was doing ballet until one day at the end of the year when we were about to write finals E TV came to me and asked me to do a thing and we did a show and somebody saw …and then he says to me I am pretty sure I saw you on TV last night but I am going to keep it a secret I don’t know if anyone has seen it, but I am pretty sure I saw you on TV last night you do ballet…

V/O
Only four years after starting ballet, 19 year old Andile was offered a scholarship at the Washington Ballet Studio.

Charla Genn
Master Ballet Coach
Charla: I was judging at the very first SA international Ballet Competition and Andile was competing and he was astonishing both in his technique and his personality and he won the award the gold medal for the contemporary and the Director of the WB was also a judge in the competition and just fell in love with him and invited him to come to W to the WB.

V/O
Charla Genn is is another South African star export. She is on the faculty of the Juillard, School of Music and Dance. Whilst Andile lives in Washington, he regularly comes to New York to be coached by Charla.

Devi Did you click instantly
Charla: Yes He is just the most adorable wonderful person to work with and actually I don’t know many dancers that work as hard as Andile he sets very high stds for himself and he will work and work until he gets it sometimes he works too much..

Devi: Watching you today and the way you rehearse and have to go over and over that’s not easy to do day in and day out and you are hard on yours self
Andile: Yes I am hard on myself extremely so because I want to do better if I don’t do better I go home and think …whats going to happen tomorrow tomorrow I have to do better so that’s how I am and if you want to do this……when you get to professional part that’s when you enjoy dancing but the process that is the part you have to stick to.

V/O
Charla Genn has a resume that reads like a Who’s Who of ballet, she has danced and choreographed around the world.

Devi: You are amazing in your own right you are hearing impaired but you hear the music you feel the music I watched you in rehearsal with Andile today how do you do that?
Charla The great thing is the hearing aids have got a lot better and I do have a 70% loss and I am very focused on the music and I guess because of my loss of hearing I have made it up with my eyes so I see a lot that a lot of people don’t see, A lot of dancers that I work with say how did you see that …obvious to me.

V/O
Andile is now in his seventh season with the Washington Ballet.
And he’s danced his way through some breath taking roles. Andile’s reputation grows with every curtain call.

Andile: It’s a joy that I don’t think anyone could understand its like you just want to fly you get on stage and you want to go everywhere on that stage and it’s like it is the most liberating thing ever.

Charla: Andile is getting better and better. This year he danced a ballet about the life of Mandela and Andile was Mandela and his acting and his command of the character was unbelievable and he brought the house down at the Kennedy Centre Opera House.

Devi: He’s not by any stretch of the imagination a small time dancer?
Charla: Not at all he’s a top international dancer I wolld say that he’s one of the best male dancers ever to come out of South Africa. He can perform anywhere and hold any stage anywhere in the world
Devi: How does that make you feel?
Charla: I don’t really know if there is another word besides proud but I am so proud of his achievement and the way he just gets better and better and not only that he has the most wonderful ability to choreograph and he choreographs his own solos and when he stops dancing I am sure he will become an international choreographer.

V/O
Early September, Andile will be back in South Africa to perform in the International Ballet Gala in Cape Town, Johannesburg, and Limpopo.

Devi: We’re sitting here at the Juilliard in NY, You dance for the Washington Ballet you stand on those stages, do you sometimes pinch yourself?
I do because I know who has been on those stages and every time I go to every theatre I know who has danced here and its Baryshnikov, Nureyev, and I am standing on the stage they danced on and that for me is a dream come true.
